_comment: CIRCUITY CALIBRATION SAMPLE. 13 real road distances against the great-circle distance
between the same two nodes, measured 2026-08-12.
PROVENANCE AND LICENCE. `roadKm` and `roadHours` come from a routing service whose network
is OSM-derived. Thirteen lookups is comfortably inside the OSMF Substantial Guideline's
'less than 100 Features' line, so this is an insubstantial extraction and no ODbL
obligation attaches. It is used ONLY to fit a single scalar. No OSM value is shipped: the
generated edges carry great-circle distance times that scalar, computed from GeoNames
coordinates. See docs/geo-data-licensing.md.
Pairs are EDGES OF THE ACTUAL SLICE, stratified by terrainDifficulty, so the residual
measures the thing the generator produces rather than an unrelated benchmark.
WHAT IT SHOWED, and it contradicted the plan:
circuity mean 1.388, p50 1.387, range 1.111 to 1.773
single global factor 1.39 -> mean |err| 12.3%, p50 11.6%, p90 21.8%
per-terrain-class factors -> mean 10.3% but p90 31.5% and max 37.5%
Per-class is WORSE at the tail. terrainDifficulty does not predict circuity — the spread
inside a class is as wide as the spread between classes, and with three samples per class
the per-class medians are fitting noise. One global factor it is.
n=13 is small and a p90 from thirteen samples is one data point. The direction is
consistent, but treat 21.8% as indicative. Widening this file is the cheapest way to firm
it up, and the format below is what --stage=calibrate will read.
